title: P01 loop-then-untie: three 320-wide Peri-LN blocks cycled A-B-C-A-B-C during pretraining, deep-copied into six untied blocks at handoff (7,474,560 params) on the 136-fable MTP Lean incumbent
description: Idea ID: P01 (looped architectures), the untie-at-handoff variant: pretraining trains N_UNIQUE=3 unique Peri-LN blocks applied in a cycle A-B-C-A-B-C (six logical applications, as 125-fable/134-fable did) at width 320 (10 heads of 32, 5 ALiBi + 5 NoPE, d_ff 1280, 3,771,840 unique params, 1.56x the per-application FLOPs of the 256-wide incumbent) with the unchanged Muon/AdamW recipe and 320-wide MTP module; when pretrain() returns, the second cycle's entries are replaced by deep copies, so RL fine-tunes six untied blocks (7,474,560 params, under the 10M cap) whose function at handoff is exactly the looped model's. It should help expert iteration because 134-fable showed a wide shared cycle hands RL a BETTER round-1 sampler than the untied 256-wide model (670 vs 647 targets) and lost only in the per-round climb, and 144-fable showed the second pass is worth ~+156 over the same blocks applied once; untying removes the summed six-application gradient on each shared block during the RL fine-tune (134's suspected drag) while keeping the looped pretraining that made the better sampler. Not what 144-claude is running (MTP weight 0.6).
hypothesis: Two observations from the loop table: (1) shared wide blocks are a good pretrain-to-RL start (134: harvest +23 with a third fewer steps; 144-fable: the same wide blocks untied and applied once lose 181), and (2) every fixed-depth loop lost its margin in the r1->r4 climb (134: +453 vs +478; 125: round-4 1098 vs 1106), where the harness's AdamW fine-tune pushes each shared block with the sum of six applications' gradients, so the two passes cannot specialise on the longer (7-16 line) RL targets the way six untied blocks can. Mechanism: pretrain in the shared regime (a depth-robust operator, cheap in unique parameters, so width is affordable), then hand RL the same function with the weight-tying constraint released; the copies start identical and diverge under the RL gradient, so the model keeps 134's round-1 harvest and gets an untied climb. This is 140-fable's G_stack idea applied at the handoff boundary instead of at 1/3 of pretraining (140 lost 37 because untied training at width 256 was already affordable and the stacking bought nothing; here the loop is what makes width 320 affordable in the 300 s budget, and the untying is what RL, not pretraining, exploits). Mechanism checks: pretraining steps 2,600-3,100 (136: 3,370; 134 at 2.25x FLOPs: 2,850); final main val loss 0.076-0.092; held-out greedy 0.95-0.975; log line 'untied to 6 blocks, 7,474,560 params at handoff'; round-1 targets solved 520-760 (136: 577/529/662) with round-1 sample acc 0.12-0.30; the decisive check is the climb: r1->r4 mean >= +480 and round-4 targets >= 1,110 (136: 1102/1114/1124; 134: 1159/1115/1095). Failure modes: (a) size, not sharing, slowed 134's climb (102/103: >5.4M-param models climbed slower in later rounds), so the 7.47M untied model climbs no faster and nets <= 0; (b) 600 AdamW steps per round at 3e-4 barely separate identical copies, so RL sees a de facto shared model and the result repeats 134's -13; (c) the 320-wide MTP module plus 1.56x FLOPs leaves fewer than 2,600 steps and a weaker round 1; (d) the 5+5 head split with 5-head ALiBi slopes (1/3.03..1/256; 119-claude's 5-of-8 lost 14 at width 256) costs a few theorems independently of the loop. Timing: width cost little in 134 (totals 1,707-1,856 s at 384 wide), predicted totals 1,550-1,950 s, no timeout.
expected_delta: -45 to +40 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean), central +5; keep needs > 658

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, forward via features() as in 136; CHANGED: pretraining builds 3 unique PeriLNBlock objects listed twice in model.blocks (A-B-C-A-B-C, six logical applications); at the end of pretrain() entries 3-5 are replaced by copy.deepcopy of entries 0-2, so the handoff model has 6 untied blocks with the looped model's exact function (CPU check: max abs logit diff 0.0 before/after untie; cached vs full forward max abs diff 1.1e-6 after untie; 0 parameters without grad after untie)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope, same construction as 115-fable with N_HEAD=10: no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/5) = 0.3299, 0.1088, 0.0359, 0.0118, 0.0039 for heads 1..5 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 5 heads) and 0 for heads 6..10 (NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 136-fable: d_model 256 -> 320 (head dim 32 kept, 8 -> 10 heads, d_ff 4x = 1280), pretraining with 3 unique blocks cycled twice instead of 6 untied blocks, untied at handoff. The RL/sampled model is a plain 6-block ALiBiGPT/PeriLNBlock stack of width 320; forward, features(), KV-cache handling and the MTP module (now 320 wide, pretraining only) are otherwise unchanged
arch.n_params_detail: handoff model: 6 x 1,234,240 (PeriLNBlock at d=320: 12*320^2 = 1,228,800 weights + 2,880 projection biases + 2,560 Peri-LN params) + emb 107*320 + head 107*320 = 68,480 + ln_f 640 = 7,474,560 (CPU check with a 130-token stub vocab gave 7,489,280 = the same formula). During pretraining the trunk has 3,771,840 unique params (3 blocks) and the separate MTP module 1,440,320 (PeriLNBlock 1,234,240 + proj (320,640) 204,800 + 2 LayerNorms 1,280); 5,212,160 trained in total, under the cap even if counted
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 320, 10) from this pretrain.py with six PeriLNBlock(320, 10) blocks, then load state: entries 3-5 are independent tensors after the untie. The MTP module is not saved
arch.kv_cache: unchanged from 115-fable/136-fable: one cache dict per model.blocks entry (six after the untie; caches[0] also holds key positions); the looped pretraining never uses caches

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial); the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (320,640) input proj) join the Muon group and its LayerNorm gains/biases and projection biases join AdamW, same lr, schedule and decay as the trunk
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock with CHANGED floor: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak (115-fable: 0.1 x peak). Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 follows the same factor, and so does its per-step decoupled decay lr * MUON_WD

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 320) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR; the reference width is the knob D, as in 134-fable at 384): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2, head (107,320) 1, MTP input proj (320,640) sqrt(2)
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor CHANGED 0.1 -> 0.3); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 13 unique trunk matrices (3 shared blocks + head.weight) + 5 MTP matrices = 18
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU (this session, stub vocab 130): looped n_params 3,786,560 with 13 unique block+head matrices; untied n_params 7,489,280 with 100 distinct parameter tensors; untie preserves logits exactly; cached vs full forward max abs diff 1.1e-6; every parameter receives a gradient after the untie

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 18 Muon matrices (13 trunk + 5 MTP) including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: during pretraining 13 unique trunk matrices (3 shared blocks x (qkv split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) + head.weight; model.blocks.parameters() deduplicates the twice-listed blocks by identity, CPU check: 13) plus the MTP module's 5 (qkv split, proj, fc1, fc2, input proj (320,640)): 18 Muon matrices; the handoff model's 6 untied blocks never see a pretraining optimizer state (RL creates its own AdamW)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by 3 PeriLNBlock(320, 10) objects listed twice and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every unique 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0. The MTP module (320 wide) gets the same treatment. Handoff init for RL: blocks 3-5 are exact copies of blocks 0-2 (the looped solution), so the untied model starts at the looped model's function and the copies diverge only under the RL gradient

loss.main: the fork's loss_on through the looped trunk (3 unique blocks, 6 applications): next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged definition; val_loss and train_loss/last_loss use this term only)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one 320-wide Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]
